title: A Competing-Hazards Systematization of Loss of Control in Autonomous Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.38411v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Leading AI developers have reported agents acting beyond their approved limits, which a United Nations panel described as an early warning of loss of human control. Yet incident reports and agent-safety evaluations describe these events differently, making it difficult to compare failures, trace risk across attempts, or separate agent behavior from the environment's role in allowing an out-of-scope action to succeed. To address this gap, we introduce a common framework in which each attempt ends in approved completion, safe stopping, scope escape, or continuation. We formalize the framework as a discrete-time competing-hazards model and derive escape probability within a retry budget, a model-conditional safe-budget limit, and conditions for estimation from execution logs. translated_title: 自主智能体失控问题的竞争风险系统化框架
translated_abstract: 领先的AI开发商已报告智能体出现超出其获批权限范围的行为，联合国一个专门小组将其描述为人类失去控制权的早期预警。然而，事故报告与智能体安全评估对这些事件的描述方式各不相同，导致难以比较各类故障、跨多次尝试追踪风险，或将智能体行为与环境在使越权行动得以成功中所起的作用区分开来。为填补这一空白，我们引入了一个统一框架，其中每次尝试以四种结果之一结束：获批完成、安全停止、越界逃脱或继续运行。我们将该框架形式化为离散时间竞争风险模型，并推导出重试预算内的逃脱概率、模型条件下的安全预算上限，以及从执行日志中进行估计的条件。我们基于一手资料，审计了2025年1月至2026年9月间发布的22份事故报告和102项智能体安全评估。其中六起事故涉及的任务……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将自主智能体的失控问题形式化为离散时间竞争风险模型，用统一框架系统化审计事故报告与安全评估，并推导出逃脱概率与安全预算上限等可量化的风险指标。
en_tdlr: This paper systematizes loss of control in autonomous agents as a discrete-time competing-hazards model, unifying the analysis of incident reports and safety evaluations while deriving escape probabilities and safe-budget limits.
